item.meaning: The sensory adaptation of emitting high-frequency ultrasonic sound waves and listening to returning echoes to navigate, detect obstacles, and hunt in turbid environment.
A low-lying wetland landform created at the mouth of a river where it slows down, deposits fine silt and sediment, and empties into an ocean or sea.

item.definition: A massive civil barrier constructed across a river course to store flowing water in artificial reservoirs for domestic supply, irrigation, and hydroelectric generation.

item.title: River Gradient & Sedimentation Profile
item.description: High water velocity on steep mountain slopes causes channel erosion and sediment transport. Upon reaching flat plains, water slows down, depositing fine silt to form fertile alluvial plains and deltas.

item.title: Ultrasonic Echolocation in Turbid Waters
item.description: Blind Ganges river dolphins emit high-frequency sound waves that bounce off underwater objects and return as echoes, providing precise 3D spatial mapping in muddy rivers.

item.function: Emits ultrasonic sound pulses and interprets returning echoes to locate fish and navigate in muddy river water where eyes are functionless.

item.cause: Turbid, muddy water conditions in peninsular and Himalayan river basins.
item.effect: The Ganges river dolphin evolved functional blindness and adapted echolocation sonar for navigation and hunting.

item.relationship_nature: Inverse Relationship with Sedimentation: Steep mountain slopes produce high water velocity and land erosion; gentle plain gradients reduce river speed, causing sediment deposition and delta formation.

procedure: 1. Build a sloped soil hill inside an inclined tray.
2. Pour water steadily from the top ridge to represent a mountain river origin.
3. Observe where rocks, sand, and fine silt are deposited as water flows downhill onto the flat base.
item.inference: Fast water on steep slopes carries heavy sediments; as slope flattens and water velocity decreases, sediment settles to form delta-like deposits.
